name: ui/toaster
title: Toaster
summary: A polite live region for script-light pages, with one inline script that defines `window.toast(message, kind?)`: each toast is appended to the region and leaves after `duration` ms.

props.name: duration
props.description: How long each toast stays, in milliseconds (data-duration).

behaviour: Renders an empty `<div id="toaster" role="status" aria-live="polite">`, fixed at the bottom of the viewport, so a toast added later is announced.
Its inline script defines `window.toast(msg, kind)`: it appends a `data-slot="toast"` card with the message as text (never HTML) and removes it after `data-duration` ms (5000 if unset).
`kind === "error"` gives the toast a `--destructive` border; any other kind a `--border` one.
The region ignores pointer events; each toast takes them.
The React build renders the same region and exports `toast(message, kind?)`, which does what the Astro script's `window.toast` does; once mounted it also sets `window.toast`.

keyboard: None: toasts are announcements, not controls.
aria: role="status" with aria-live="polite", rendered empty so later toasts are announced.

theming.brandOverlay: None. The toast is `--card` with a `--border` (or `--destructive` for errors) in every brand.

noJs.without: The empty live region renders; with no script there is no `window.toast`, so a page shows its messages in its own markup instead.
noJs.with: `window.toast(message, kind?)` shows a toast in the live region for `duration` ms.

responsive: Full width less 16px gutters at the bottom on phones, toasts centred; from sm, bottom-right 24px in, toasts right-aligned, each at most 24rem.
contract:
contract
  slot is "toaster"
  role is "status"
  when quick slot is "toaster"
  when quick role is "status"
end

checks.say: One polite live region, addressed by id.
The duration is carried to the script.
The region renders empty: no toast until the script adds one.

gaps: Toasts leave after `duration` ms with no way to pause, extend or dismiss them: WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable) is not met for a message a reader needs; prefer `app/toast` (no timeout) for those.
The region's id is fixed (`toaster`), so one Toaster per page; a second would collide.

`window.toast` is a global, and the toast markup is built by script, so the contract runners (which do not execute scripts) cannot check it; `__tests__/components/toaster.test.tsx` checks the React `toast()` instead.
